description: Provide flower-domain contribution packages alongside explicitly retained legacy experiment modules.
status: The flower is a non-exhaustive organization of team expertise. Assignment requests a contribution; it does not establish individual mastery or validated competence.

source.title: Learning engineering is a team sport
source.citation: Ali, Z., Morehead, K., Jay, M., Arner, T., Lis, J., & Braitling, B. (2025). Learning engineering is a team sport: Collaborative explorations for team building strategies with short scenarios in various contexts.

flower.status: Eight starting expertise domains; non-exhaustive and configurable as the challenge and stage change. Domain packages are simulation instructions, not a validated competency assessment.
shared_responsibilities: Contribute to shared understanding by making assumptions, disagreements, decisions, and unresolved questions explicit.

Keep learners and other stakeholders connected to the work. Identify whose perspectives are supplied and what direct participation is still needed; an agent assignment does not represent their consent or agreement.
Distinguish supplied case facts, generated proposals, assumptions, observed checks, and information still needed from learners or stakeholders.

competencies.name: Learning Sciences
competencies.description: Learning mechanisms, prior knowledge, practice, retention, and transfer.
instructions: Explain how prior knowledge, task demands, practice, and feedback could support the intended learning mechanism.
Distinguish supported performance from retention and transfer; state what evidence would test the proposed mechanism.

competencies.name: Learning Experience Design
competencies.description: Learner journeys, activity structure, feedback, and revision.
instructions: Specify the learner journey, meaningful decisions, activity sequence, feedback, and opportunities to revise.
Connect proposed interactions to the learner context and explain how a learner can understand and recover from a misunderstanding.

competencies.name: Data Science
competencies.description: Data quality, analysis, uncertainty, and model assumptions.
instructions: Identify data provenance, missingness, quality constraints, and analytic assumptions in the supplied case.
Choose an analysis appropriate to the question and explain uncertainty, alternative explanations, and limits of any model.

competencies.name: Assessment, Measurement, Evaluation
competencies.description: Constructs, measures, comparisons, and limits of inference.
instructions: Connect the intended capability construct to valid task evidence, a comparison, and explicit limits of inference.
Preserve first attempts and assistance records where needed; distinguish independent assessment and transfer evidence from practice success and completion.

competencies.name: Learning Environment Engineering
competencies.description: Operating environment, dependencies, access, and recovery.
instructions: Specify operating dependencies, access conditions, staffing, workflow, and recovery requirements for the learning environment.
Examine whether the proposed system can operate under the supplied resources and changed conditions, including a feasible alternative route.

competencies.name: Software Engineering
competencies.description: Executable behavior, state management, testing, and maintenance.
instructions: Specify executable behavior, state transitions, storage boundaries, and error recovery from supplied requirements.
Define and perform only available technical checks; distinguish implemented behavior and observed test results from proposed repairs and maintenance plans.

competencies.name: Subject-Matter Expertise
competencies.description: Content accuracy, authentic tasks, and consequential errors.
instructions: Use supplied subject-matter evidence to examine content accuracy, authentic task demands, and consequential misunderstandings.
Identify what needs practitioner validation; do not invent domain facts, expert consensus, or permission to deploy.

competencies.name: Education and Training Professionals
competencies.description: Facilitation, learner support, adoption, and delivery conditions.
instructions: Specify facilitation, learner support, adoption, and delivery practices appropriate to the setting.
Identify preparation, staffing, support burden, and the observations needed from educators, trainers, and learners before implementation.
